title: Get Others to Do the Work for You, Always Take the Credit
summary: Life is short and time must be saved, so rather than exhausting yourself doing all the work, hire or use the efforts and past works of others while securing the credit for yourself. Credit builds your aura and reputation, making you seem important. Protect yourself from vultures who steal work, but join them when your position allows to work smart instead of hard.
example: Thomas Edison took credit, money, and fame for Nikola Tesla's hardworking inventions and AC system, leaving Tesla with very little.
The original father of radio used Tesla's patents, depriving Tesla of fame and money because Tesla did not know how to protect his work.
Politicians receive credit for speeches written by ghostwriters.
reversal: Taking credit can backfire and destroy your reputation if people find out the truth, as seen when Edison's reputation suffered after his death.
Only take credit when your position is unshakable.
If it serves your purpose, give credit to your master to show loyalty rather than stealing the limelight, aligning with Law 1.
